_comment: How this language's pronunciation becomes its transliteration. Read by lib/translit.py; optional, like every file of this name. Arabic has no `map`: the source's own romanisation is already the scheme docs/lang/ar.md uses, in all but four letters and one habit, and those are what `roman` fixes.
_roman: Wiktionary writes hamza and ʿayn with the IPA letters ʔ and ʕ, and x and ġ with an underlined k and a macron g; docs/lang/ar.md writes ʾ ʿ ḫ ġ. Unfixed, a video's verb line read `أَرَى ʔarā`, `يَبْعَدُ yabʕadu`, and the sidebar's \dw wrote `ḵaraja`. `drop_initial` is the hamza every word that begins with a vowel carries in the source (أَسْتَطِيعُ ʔastaṭīʕu) and that the edition does not write at the start of a word: astaṭīʿu. Inside a word it is a consonant and stays (saʾala). lib/verbs/ar.py respells its own slots the same way, and applying both changes nothing twice.
_pausal: Not read for standard Arabic: the rule a variety's file turns on with `from_standard.pausal` (lib/translit.py pausal), so that a standard dictionary hit shown in a dialect text loses its final case vowel and tanwīn, as every dialect and standard Arabic's own pausal reading do (kataba > katab, kitābun > kitāb, madrasatun > madrasa). `verb` and `noun` are the parts of speech it reads (a pronoun, a particle and an adverb are left as written); `short` the vowels it cuts, `long` the ones it keeps; `tanwin` the nunated endings; `feminine` the letter whose -a stays (ة); `verb_keep` the verb ending after a consonant that is a pronoun and stays (the feminine plural's -na, katabna); `contract` the -iy and -uw a cut leaves, written as the long vowel they are (qawiya > qawī). A noun entry's own romanisation is never cut: the dictionary writes it without an ending. One rule for all four dialects: their own vowels and stress are left to the dialect dictionaries' own romanisation (docs/lang/ar.md).
